title: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations
abstract: arXiv:2610.40759v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Musicians and mixing engineers often can decipher the signal processing chain they hear on a reference recording, then adapt it to new material. We present TAPE (Transformations of Audio Parameter Embeddings), which estimates this processing from the processed reference audio alone. An encoder trained to identify processors in eight major effect families maps the reference to an embedding. A differentiable digital signal processing (DSP) chain decodes the embedding into editable parameters in one forward pass and applies them to a different unprocessed recording. Its modules are equalization, compression, waveshaping, a small residual network, and reverberation. TAPE achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST, the previous state of the art for single-step regression, and lower spectral error than per-example search over a chain approximating ST-ITO's, while running 275$\times$ faster than that search. tldr: TAPE提出仅凭处理后的参考音频即可通过编码器与可微分DSP链一次性解码出可编辑的音频效果参数，在频谱误差上超越现有最先进方法，同时速度比基于搜索的方法快275倍。
en_tdlr: TAPE estimates the signal processing chain from processed reference audio alone by mapping it to an embedding via an encoder and decoding it into editable DSP parameters in one forward pass, achieving lower spectral error than prior state-of-the-art methods while running 275× faster than search-based approaches.
